Subject: Sudden latency + 5xx spike affecting our reserved pool

Hi Chloe —

We started seeing a sharp latency increase and a stream of 5xx responses from your dedicated pool at ~11:05 UTC. This is impacting our customer-facing inference endpoint (prod). Throughput drops to ~40% of our reserved baseline and p95 latency has jumped from ~120ms to >1.2s.

We have a Reserved capacity contract (FP-2026-RESV-4932) so this behavior is unexpected. Attaching a short log snippet (kernel side) we pulled from our side.

Quick details:
- Window: 11:05 — ongoing
- Impact: user-facing errors (503) and high tail latency
- Our region: us-west-2
- Priority: High — revenue impact

Can you confirm if any changes were rolled to the dedicated pool or if there are known kernel/optimizations being deployed that might affect slot availability or compilation latency?

We need an ETA on mitigation. If you need access to more logs or runbooks, tell us what to pull and we’ll provide it immediately.

Thanks,
Dana Liu

Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden latency + 5xx spike affecting our reserved pool

Chloe / Marissa / FasterPay team — quick triage from infra:

What we see:
- A canary release pushed yesterday contained an experimental kernel autotuner for attention ops. It increases JIT compile attempts for longer-sequence batches to micro-optimise throughput.
- Under a burst of mixed sequence lengths (FasterPay's traffic pattern), the autotuner triggers frequent recompiles which block GPU slot hash tables and inflate kernel compile latency. Result: slow cold kernels, queue pile-up, and timeouts.

Immediate mitigations (we can run now):
1) Flip the autotuner flag off on FasterPay's dedicated pool. Command: infractl pool config set --pool fp-reserved-4932 --flag attention_autotuner=false
2) Enable the fallback precompiled kernel path for priority customers: infractl pool set --pool fp-reserved-4932 --kernel-mode precompiled
3) Throttle best-effort workloads in the same availability slice: infractl throttle set --slice shared-nonpriority --ratio 0.25

I have a short rollback playbook ready (attached). Estimated impact window after changes: 3–7 minutes to drain compilation queue and return to baseline p95. If the autotuner flip does not recover, next step is full rollback of yesterday's build (longer, ~30–45m).

I'll apply mitigation (1) now if Chloe authorizes. Also recommend we open a post-mortem to evaluate the autotuner gating for reserved pools.

Rishi
Senior Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Dana Liu <dana@fasterpay.com>, FasterPay SRE Team <sre@fasterpay.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 12:34:02 +0000
Subject: Re: Sudden latency + 5xx surge affecting our reserved pool

Dana / FasterPay team —

Thank you for the quick heads up and the logs. We identified an interaction between a kernel autotuner we shipped yesterday and your traffic mix: the autotuner is causing repeated JIT/compile stalls and blocking GPU slot reuse which is manifesting as the throughput shortfall and 5xxs you saw.

What we've done so far:
- Flipped attention_autotuner=false on your dedicated pool (fp-reserved-4932).
- Switched the pool to precompiled kernel mode for higher predictability.
- Throttled non-priority shared slices to free headroom for your reserved capacity.

Current status: our metrics show compilation queue draining and p95 trending back toward baseline. We expect stabilization within 10 minutes; if not, Rishi will trigger a full rollback of the canary build (he's standing by).

Next steps & offers:
- I'll run a short exec-level readout at 13:00 UTC if you'd like to join (15 min).
- We will include a formal SLA impact assessment and propose a make-good (credits/burst) if we confirm measurable downtime. Marissa, please own the customer-facing SLA summary and proposal.

Apologies for the interruption and thank you for your patience — we're prioritizing your capacity and I'll keep you updated every 10 minutes until fully stabilized.

Chloe Martin
